Multiple shadows components can be set for a single object. There are 4 light sources in this scene, each resulting in a separate shadow of the object.

This demonstrates how Swift Shadows can be used on uneven surfaces like terrain.
    "Use two cameras" enables drawing the character and shadow on a separate pass, which eliminates the effect of shadow being clipped with terrain. This comes with the cost of some possible artifacts that aren't noticeable for most situations.

This is a generic demonstration of what Swift Shadows can do.
    A raycast from the light source to the cubes determines the position of shadow, and a projected quad is rendered in place. All shadows are drawn with a single draw call, which is especially useful for mobile devices.
    You can also notice the limitation: shadows are casted on one surface at time and can extend beyond the surface they are projected on. Shadows can be set to fade away as they fall at extreme angles to make this effect less noticeable.

This is an example of a more creative use of Swift Shadows, with hundreds of shadow objects calculated and drawn at the same time. All light spots use a special "light" material and are rendered within a single draw call.

This scene demonstrates shadows following the transform of object they are attached to. In this scene, the blades and body of helicopter, as well as the platform and dish of the radar station, are actually two different overlayed shadows. Nevertheless, the shadows are still drawn in a single draw call by using a texture atlas.

On Android, Firebase requires C/C++ and Java components
that are distributed with the Firebase and Android SDKs.

It's likely the required dependencies for Firebase were not included
in your Unity project.
Assets/Plugins/Android/ in your Unity project should contain
AAR files in the form firebase-*.aar
You may have disabled the Android Resolver which would
have added the AAR dependencies for you.

Do the following to enable the Android Resolver in Unity:
* Select the menu option 'Assets -> Play Services Resolver -> 
  Android Resolver -> Settings'
* In the Android Resolver settings check
  'Enable Background Resolution'
* Select the menu option 'Assets -> Play Services Resolver ->
  Android Resolver -> Resolve Client Jars' to force Android
  dependency resolution.
* Rebuild your APK and deploy.

On iOS and tvOS Firebase requires native (C/C++) and Cocoapod
components that are distributed with the Firebase SDK and via
Cocoapods.

It's likely that you did not include the require Cocoapod
dependencies for Firebase in your Unity project.
You may have disabled the iOS Resolver which would have added
the Cocoapod dependencies for you.

Do the following to enable the iOS Resolver in Unity:
* Select the menu option 'Assets -> Play Services Resolver ->
  iOS Resolver -> Settings'
* In the iOS Resolver settings check 'Podfile Generation' and
  'Add Cocoapods to Generated Xcode Project'.
* Build your iOS or tvOS project and check the Unity console for
  any errors associated with Cocoapod tool execution.
  You will need to correctly install Cocoapods tools to generate
  a working build.
